subject: WeightsHub mirror & redistribution policy — initial terms
messages:
From: Elena Duarte <elena@weightshub.org>
To: partnerships@redwood-inference.com
Cc: legal@weightshub.org
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: WeightsHub proposal — mirrored weights distribution model

Hi Redwood partnerships team,

Thanks for the quick connect at the Model Ecosystem Summit last week. I’m Elena, Head of Publisher Relations at WeightsHub. We publish a range of open models under permissive but attribution-aware licenses and we’ve had a growing number of partner requests to mirror and redistribute pre-packaged weights behind partner endpoints (cached/mirrored copies) to improve access latency and resiliency in regions we don’t serve directly.

High-level ask: can Redwood operate a mirrored copy of select WeightsHub model weights (we’d define a whitelist) and redistribute them to Redwood customers under a limited redistribution right and attribution requirements? We’d need:
- Verified attribution metadata embedded in manifests
- Controls to prevent downstream relicensing (no sublicensing)
- Export-control & compliance carveouts if model includes restricted components

I’ve attached our current publisher license (weightshub_license_v1.pdf) and a brief one-pager.

If this is interesting, can we get a short call next week to align on legal guardrails and an operational checklist?

Thanks,
Elena Duarte
Head of Publisher Relations
WeightsHub
Attachments: weightshub_license_v1.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elena Duarte <elena@weightshub.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: WeightsHub proposal — mirrored weights distribution model

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for sending the license. I’m Rishi (partnerships at Redwood). We’re interested; this aligns with a number of partner-led distribution plays we’ve been exploring. A few clarifying questions up front so we scope the integration correctly:

1) Scope: do you expect Redwood to serve the full weight files to end customers (i.e., host and return model binaries) or only host trimmed/quantized variants?
2) Attribution: you mention embedded manifests — can you share an example of the metadata fields and where you expect the attribution to appear in logs and manifests?
3) Term/Revocation: what revocation or takedown process do you need for discovered misuse?
4) Pricing/Cost: is there a revenue share or flat fee expected for mirrored redistribution?

Looping in Marissa from our partner GTM team to coordinate commercial and go-to-market constraints. I’ve attached a short partner intake sheet we use to map technical, legal, and go-to-market requirements (redwood-partner-matrix.xlsx).

We can do a 30-minute sync on Tue or Wed next week — preferred windows are 10–12 PT.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Partnerships (Acting)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-partner-matrix.xlsx

Thanks, Rishi — great list. To answer quickly:
- Scope: We’re happy for Redwood to host both full and quantized variants. We publish both; we’re primarily asking for a mirrored copy of the canonical weights plus optional lightweight quantized variants for cost-sensitive tiers.
- Attribution: sample manifest fields are in the attached draft (mirror_terms_draft.docx) — we require a \"publisher\" and \"model_origin\" tag in the model manifest and an attribution line in any UI or API response metadata that surfaces model provenance (e.g., \"Model: gptx-small (WeightsHub)\").
- Revocation: We propose 48-hour takedown on verified misuse; emergency takedown for export-control violations.
- Commercials: Our publishers typically ask for a modest revenue share on repackaged distributions (5–10%) or an annual distribution license if Redwood prefers fixed fees.

We attached a draft of suggested mirror terms to head off back-and-forths. Would love to do a call Tuesday 10:30 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite if that works.

Regards,
Elena Duarte
Head of Publisher Relations
WeightsHub
Attachments: mirror_terms_draft.docx

Elena — thanks for the clarifications and for the draft terms. Quick internal summary and proposed next steps:

Summary (internal):
- WeightsHub is open to allowing mirrored redistribution under attribution and revocation guardrails. They prefer either revenue share (5–10%) or an annual license.
- Operational asks: manifest attribution fields, takedown SLA (48 hours), and a carveout for export-control/emergency takedown.

Proposed next steps (external + internal):
1) Legal: I’ll send the mirror_terms_draft.docx to our legal team for a short redline. (Marissa, can you confirm who on legal should be actioned?)
2) Technical: Sergio, please scope storage/traffic implications for hosting full weights vs quantized variants and estimate monthly incremental egress/storage for a pilot of 10 models. Please add that to the intake sheet.
3) Commercial: Marissa, can you draft a revenue-share vs fixed-license comparison with estimated 12-mo economics and proposed pilot pricing?
4) Schedule: Elena, we’re good for Tue 10:30 PT — go ahead and send the invite.

I’ll mark this as high priority internally — this could become a standard publisher alliance pattern for us if we can standardize manifests and takedown flows.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Partnerships (Acting)
Redwood Inference
